name: fig32_unitary_vs_nonunitary_evaporation
caption: Toy evaporation of an N = 10 qubit register: each step applies a Haar-random unitary to the remaining black-hole qubits and then emits one qubit. (a) Unitary evolution reproduces the Page curve (mean over 24 seeds vs the exact average); the non-unitary reference (each emitted qubit is traced out of a mixed register and discarded from correlations) gives the monotonic Hawking-like S(R) = k ln 2. (b) The unitary global state stays pure (max norm deviation 8.9e-16); the non-unitary one becomes mixed. (c) The mutual information between radiation and black hole is 2 S(R) in the unitary model and zero in the reference. Non-unitary averages use 4 seeds. This is a qubit toy model, not a gravitational calculation.
